identity.title: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents

problem.claim: Evaluate vision-driven embodied agents built with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) across real-world task abilities.

gap.claim: MLLM-based embodied agents are underexplored because comprehensive evaluation frameworks are lacking.

contributions.claim: Introduces EmbodiedBench, with 1,128 tasks across four environments and six capability-focused subsets spanning reasoning, instruction understanding, spatial awareness, perception, and planning.
Evaluates 24 proprietary and open-source MLLMs using the benchmark.
Provides the benchmark code and dataset publicly.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish EmbodiedBench as an extensive, multifaceted standardized evaluation platform for vision-driven embodied agents.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MLLMs perform well on high-level tasks but struggle with low-level manipulation; GPT-4o, identified as the best model, scores 28.9% on average.
The authors report that benchmark evaluation highlights existing challenges and provides insights intended to advance MLLM-based embodied agents.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLM-based embodied agents are promising, but comprehensive evaluation is missing.
EmbodiedBench organizes 1,128 tasks across four environments and six capability-oriented subsets.
The benchmark is used to evaluate 24 leading proprietary and open-source MLLMs.
The authors report a high-level/low-level performance gap, with GPT-4o averaging 28.9%.
The platform is presented as a standardized way to expose challenges and guide progress, with code and data released.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates benchmark scope into environments and capability-focused subsets, then reports an aggregate model comparison and a specific low-level weakness.

lessons.interpretation: This pairing connects evaluation coverage to an interpretable capability diagnosis rather than presenting only a single leaderboard score.
lessons.application: Design evaluations with both broad task coverage and capability-specific slices, and report a concrete failure mode alongside aggregate results.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the task has no meaningful capability decomposition or when subset scores would be statistically underpowered.

unknowns: The abstract does not report per-environment or per-subset scores, task-level variance, evaluation conditions, or baselines beyond GPT-4o.
The claim that GPT-4o is the best model is not further qualified by model versions, prompting, or comparison metrics.
